messages:
Liam (AE): kicking off thread — AcmeCorp POC inbound, large EU financial customer. they require EU-only processing + customer-managed KMS. can we map out feasibility and cost impact?
Tess (SE): thanks. two quick asks from their checklist: 1) must list subprocessors in EU-only flow, 2) must confirm fallback behavior if an EU region is overloaded.
Omar (Infra): short answer: yes we can do EU-only routing for the POC. routing policy options: geofence (pin tenant to eu-west-1), tenant affinity with region pinning, or strict geofence with fail-hard. fallback options: failover to another EU region (eu-west-2) or to dedicated private deployment if capacity exceeded.
Nina (Security): important: if they want customer-managed keys (CMK) we need to confirm KMS topology. Redwood hosted KMS in EU is possible, or customer can use an external KMS via VPC peering + external key wrap. which one do they prefer?
Liam (AE): they asked for CMK in customer account (bring-your-own-key). also asked for a list of sub-processors that would touch data during EU-only flow.
Omar (Infra): for BYOK/CMK in account we support a keystore proxy; flow is: request -> private control plane (EU) -> key proxy calls customer's KMS endpoint (in EU). No plaintext leaves EU. we need a short runbook to confirm network egress rules.
Tess (SE): adding a config snippet for the POC routing policy (pseudo):
```
routing_policy: {
  mode: "tenant_pin",
  regions: ["eu-west-1"],
  failover: {type: "eu-only", targets: ["eu-west-2"], behavior: "queue_and_notify"}
}
```
Tess (SE): note: failover behavior "queue_and_notify" will queue requests if both primary & failover are saturated; fail-hard is also an option but customer prefers availability.
Elaine (Sales Ops): pricing question from procurement: if we do a dedicated EU pool for this POC (reserved), what's the delta vs hosted per-token? can we give a ballpark commit estimate?
Omar (Infra): ballpark: hosted per-token stays same, but dedicated reserved adds a baseline monthly commit. for a short POC (2-4 weeks) dedicated is usually more expensive unless they need strict isolation. I can pull numbers based on expected QPS — what's their target throughput?
Liam (AE): they want 100 QPS peak, average 30 QPS. sequences ~512 tokens typical.
Omar (Infra): ok rough calc: 100 QPS * 512 tokens * 3600s * 24h -> huge if continuous, but POC not 24/7. I'll run a quick sim tomorrow and share per-token vs reserved.
Nina (Security): on subprocessors: for EU-only path we still have infra subprocessors (cloud provider EU regions, monitoring provider in EU, optional logging infra in EU). Ivan, can you confirm legal copy for the subprocessor list?
Ivan (Legal): will compile. quick heads-up: if customer requires contractual restriction (no non-EU subprocessors at all) we may need Private deployment in their VPC or dedicated infra in EU to avoid telemetry pipelines hitting non-EU partners.
Liam (AE): customer also asked about egress logs — they want proof of no cross-border egress. can we provide packet-level proof or signed attestations?
Omar (Infra): we can provide flow logs showing egress routes and KMS audit logs for key usage. packet-level capture is heavy but possible within a support engagement. signed attestation: ops can create an export with signatures.
Tess (SE): for the POC test plan I propose: 1) week 0 — provision eu-only routing + CMK test key, 2) week 1 — run synthetic load 30/100 QPS to validate latency & KV cache behavior, 3) week 2 — failover exercise to eu-west-2, 4) week 3 — uplift to production like traffic and handoff.
Elaine (Sales Ops): procurement also asking: if failover goes to eu-west-2, is that considered "cross-region" billing? any extra egress fees?
Omar (Infra): intra-EU region routing stays within same cloud provider region construct; there's no cross-border egress charge but there could be inter-region egress costs depending on provider. we'll provide cost delta in the pricing slide.
Liam (AE): customer wants a short one-pager for execs: "Can Redwood ensure EU-only processing with BYOK and what is the POC cost and timeline?" can someone assemble?
Tess (SE): I'll draft the one-pager with technical notes and attach the routing snippet + test plan.
Ivan (Legal): I'll attach a trimmed subprocessor list and a recommended contractual clause for EU-only processing.
Nina (Security): I'll prepare the KMS audit proof template and checklist for customer pen-test constraints.
deploy-bot: POC request #ACME-482 created in ops queue. ETA for infra provisioning: 3 business days.
Elaine (Sales Ops): perfect — Liam i'll prepare the commercial outline (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and include a short example commit for 2-week dedicated POC.
Liam (AE): thanks all. next sync tomorrow at 10am CET to review the one-pager and cost slides. @Tess @Omar please bring the failover test steps. :thumbsup:
